extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and USPTO examiners (patent prosecution practitioners)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and formal requirements for preparing and examining the parts, form, and content of a U.S. utility patent application specification (title, abstract, background, summary, drawings, detailed description, claims, sequence listings, incorporation-by-reference, and related formatting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Embedded hyperlinks and browser-executable code
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclosure is objectionable if it contains an embedded hyperlink and/or other form of browser-executable code; applicant must delete embedded hyperlinks and/or other forms of browser-executable code and references to websites should be limited to the top-level domain name without any prefix such as http:// or other browser-executable code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should object to the specification and indicate applicants must delete embedded hyperlinks/browser-executable code. Exception: requirement does not apply to electronic documents listed on forms PTO-892 and PTO/SB/08 where the electronic document is identified by reference to a URL. If hyperlinks are necessary because the hyperlinks/browser-executable codes themselves (rather than contents of the linked site) are part of the invention and applicant does not intend those hyperlinks to be active links, examiners should not object; the Office will disable hyperlinks when preparing text for the USPTO web database. Examples: a URL placed between “< >” or “http://” followed by an address. Note: nucleotide/amino acid sequence data placed between “< >” are not considered hyperlinks and should not be objected to as improper incorporation by reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper incorporation by reference via hyperlinks
rubrics_metrics.description: Attempting to incorporate subject matter into the patent application by reference to a hyperlink and/or other forms of browser-executable code is considered to be an improper incorporation by reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.57(e) and MPEP § 608.01(p). If the application attempts to incorporate essential or nonessential subject matter by reference to the contents of a linked site, use form paragraph 6.19 or 6.19.01 instead. Examiner Note: distinguish between linking to content (improper incorporation) and including hyperlinks that are themselves part of the invention (permitted if not active).

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement/order of application elements
rubrics_metrics.description: The elements of the application, if applicable, should appear in a preferred order (per 37 CFR 1.77): (1) Utility application transmittal form; (2) Fee transmittal form; (3) Application Data Sheet; (4) Specification; (5) Drawings; (6) Inventor's oath or declaration; etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order set forth in 37 CFR 1.77(b) is preferable (not strictly required) when framing the nonprovisional specification. Each item should appear in upper case as section headings; if no text follows a heading, the phrase 'Not Applicable' should follow the section heading. Provisional applications are recommended to follow same general format (claims not required). Specific lists of specification sections are provided (title, cross-reference, federally sponsored research statement, joint research agreement parties, incorporation-by-reference of specific electronic files, prior disclosures, background, brief summary, brief description of drawings, detailed description, claims, abstract, sequence listing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification section headings and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Specification section headings should appear in uppercase and without underlining or bold type; if no text follows a section heading, use the phrase 'Not Applicable'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section headings should be in upper case and plain formatting. If an application data sheet is used, duplicate data need not be repeated elsewhere except where specific older rules apply (e.g., citizenship for applications filed before Sept 16, 2012). The most recent compliant ADS controls certain priority/benefit claim information for applications filed on or after Sept 16, 2012.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Data Sheet (ADS) controls and discrepancy rules
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed on or after September 16, 2012, if there is a discrepancy between the information submitted in an application data sheet and information submitted elsewhere in the application, the application data sheet will control except for the naming of inventors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Naming of inventorship is governed by 37 CFR 1.41 and changes by 37 CFR 1.48. For filings before Sept 16, 2012, different discrepancy rules apply (ADS controls except for inventors and citizenship). The most recent compliant ADS governs foreign priority/domestic benefit claims (see 37 CFR 1.76(d) and MPEP § 601.05(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation-by-reference of electronic documents (read-only discs, XML files)
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must include incorporation-by-reference statements regarding material submitted on a read-only optical disc, as a text file, or an XML file via the patent electronic filing system; the statement must identify file names, date of creation, and size in bytes for specified document types (Computer Program Listing Appendix, Sequence Listing, Large Tables, Sequence Listing XML).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.77(b)(5) and MPEP § 608.05 and related Legal Framework for Patent Electronic System. This incorporation-by-reference is required for the electronic documents to become part of the permanent USPTO records. See specific sub-items (Computer Program Listing Appendix §1.96(c); Sequence Listing §1.821(c); Large Tables §1.58(c); Sequence Listing XML §1.831(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Title of the invention requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The title should be placed at the top of the first page of the specification (unless provided in ADS). The title should be brief but technically accurate and descriptive, preferably from two to seven words, and may not contain more than 500 characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.72(a) and MPEP § 606. If title provided in ADS, it need not be repeated. Avoid overly long or non-descriptive titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background of the Invention content
rubrics_metrics.description: The Background should set forth the field of the invention and a description of the related art (including information disclosed under 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98). It should describe the state of the prior art and, where applicable, indicate problems in the prior art which are solved by the applicant’s invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Field of the Invention may paraphrase applicable CPC definitions and be directed to the subject matter of the claimed invention. Description of Related Art should include references to specific related art where appropriate and point out problems solved by the invention. See MPEP §§ 608.01(a), (p), and § 707.05(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief summary of the invention
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief summary indicating its nature and substance should precede the detailed description; the summary should be commensurate with the invention as claimed and describe the nature, operation, and purpose in clear, concise sentences or paragraphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summary should be directed to the specific invention being claimed (not mere generalities), may point out advantages or how it solves problems indicated in the Background, and should be consistent with the subject matter of the claims. The summary is distinct from the abstract and should aid future searches and understanding of the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief description of the drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: When there are drawings, there shall be a brief description of the several views of the drawings; the detailed description must refer to different views by figure numbers and to different parts by reference letters or numerals (preferably numerals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should ensure figures described in the specification are present in the drawings. If drawings show Figures 1A, 1B, 1C, the brief description must separately reference 1A, 1B, 1C rather than only 'Figure 1' or the examiner should object. See MPEP § 608.01(f) and treatment for applications filed without all figures (MPEP § 601.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed description of the invention
rubrics_metrics.description: The detailed description must describe the preferred embodiment(s) as required in 37 CFR 1.71 and should be as short and specific as necessary to describe the invention adequately and accurately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where elements/compounds/processes are conventional and widely known and their exact nature is not necessary for understanding, they should not be described in detail. For particularly complicated subject matter or where items may not be commonly known, the specification should refer to another patent or readily available publication which adequately describes the subject matter. See MPEP § 608.01(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims formatting and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim or claims must commence on a separate sheet or electronic page; where a claim sets forth a plurality of elements or steps, each element or step should be separated by a line indentation. There may be plural indentations to further segregate subcombinations or related steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.75 and MPEP § 608.01(m). Claims must be clearly presented and start on a separate page; proper indentation helps segregate elements/subcombinations and aids clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract of the disclosure: presence and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief abstract of the technical disclosure must commence on a separate sheet under the heading 'Abstract' or 'Abstract of the Disclosure'; the abstract must be as concise as the disclosure permits, preferably not exceeding 150 words, and its purpose is to enable quick determination of the nature and gist of the technical disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPAP will review applications for compliance and require an abstract if missing. Examiner should require or object early if abstract does not comply. The abstract is considered part of the specification for 35 U.S.C. 112 purposes and should be corrected by applicant when necessary. If the application is otherwise in condition for allowance except for the abstract, the examiner generally should make necessary revisions by formal examiner’s amendment after obtaining applicant’s authorization rather than issuing a Quayle action. See form paragraphs 6.12–6.16 for procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract content specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent abstract should be a concise statement of the technical disclosure and should include that which is new in the art to which the invention pertains; it should not refer to purported merits or speculative applications or compare the invention with the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent is basic in nature the abstract may be directed to the entire disclosure; for improvements it should include the technical disclosure of the improvement. Where applicable, include: (1) machine/apparatus—organization and operation; (2) article—method of making; (3) chemical compound—identity and use; (4) mixture—ingredients; (5) process—the steps. Extensive mechanical/design details should not be included. In chemical cases, give general nature and use and exemplify species if illustrative. The abstract should be narrative and generally a single paragraph of 50–150 words (preferably) and not exceed 15 lines. Avoid legal phraseology and claim-style terminology such as 'means' and 'said', and avoid repeating the title or using implied phrases like 'This disclosure concerns'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract language and format requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract must commence on a separate sheet (preferably following the claims), be in narrative form, generally limited to a single paragraph within 50–150 words, and should not include other parts of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use heading 'Abstract' or 'Abstract of the Disclosure'. If the abstract does not commence on a separate sheet, require a new abstract on a separate sheet (form paragraph 6.16.01). The abstract should describe the disclosure sufficiently to assist readers in deciding whether to consult the full patent text. Examiner may require correction in first Office action or at earliest point noted; replies are treated under 37 CFR 1.111(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraphs for abstract deficiencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific form paragraphs exist for examiner use when abstract is missing or objected to (¶ 6.12 Abstract Missing; ¶ 6.13 Abstract Objected To; ¶ 6.14 Content; ¶ 6.15 Chemical Cases; ¶ 6.16 Language; ¶ 6.16.01 Placement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 6.12 when abstract is missing (with examiner notes for pro se applicants and national stage exceptions). Use 6.13 to indicate required corrections and specify defects (e.g., legal phraseology, undue length). Use 6.14–6.16 to remind applicant of proper content, chemical specifics, language, and placement. Examiner Notes indicate when to follow up with additional form paragraphs for pro se applicants and national stage exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing requirements and format
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'Sequence Listing' is required when the application discloses nucleotide or amino acid sequences; the listing is required whether sequences are claimed or not and must be submitted in required formats (e.g., ASCII text file via PES or as specified PDF/electronic submissions per 37 CFR 1.821–1.825).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence Listing required on paper if not submitted electronically as specified. See MPEP §§ 2421–2431 and 37 CFR 1.821–1.825 for submission details. Note earlier statement that nucleotide/amino acid sequence data placed between '< >' are not considered hyperlinks and should not be objected to.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings and photographs standards (black & white, color, photographs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Black and white drawings are normally required (India ink or equivalent). Color drawings are permitted in design applications and, on rare occasions, in utility applications if color is the only practical medium; photographs are not ordinarily permitted but allowed if they are the only practicable medium for illustrating the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Color drawings in utility applications require a petition with fee (§ 1.17(h)), submission of specified sets of color drawings, and insertion of specific language in the brief description of drawings stating that the file contains color drawings and that copies with color drawings will be provided upon request and fee. Color drawings must be reproducible in black and white in the printed patent and are not permitted in international applications (PCT Rule 11.13). Photographs (black & white or color) are acceptable for certain subject matter (e.g., electrophoresis gels, blots, cell cultures, histological sections, animals, plants, in vivo imaging, TLC plates, crystalline structures, ornamental effects) and must be of sufficient quality so all details are reproducible in the printed patent. If the subject admits illustration by a drawing, the examiner may require a drawing instead of a photograph. See 37 CFR 1.84 and relevant MPEP paragraphs.
